# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is the **technical manual** for PhyloTrace — the reference for people who
work *on* the application rather than *with* it. It documents the code as it is
actually written: how the program boots, how it is divided into modules, how
those modules communicate, what the database file contains, how each component
is implemented, and what a change to any of them has to respect.

It is the companion to the **user manual** (`docs/manual/`), which explains what
PhyloTrace does and how to use it, in plain language and without R. The two books
are deliberately separate: the user manual assumes no programming background at
all, so every implementation detail it used to carry has been moved here.

## Who this book is for {.unnumbered}

Developers and maintainers who need the *how*: the module hierarchy, the reactive
signal bus, the database schema, the exact functions that build a distance
matrix or shell out to the typing toolchain — cited directly from the source.

If you want to know what a minimum spanning tree *is*, why allelic distance is a
meaningful measure of relatedness, or how to run an outbreak investigation in the
app, read the user manual instead. This book assumes those questions are already
answered.

## How to read it {.unnumbered}

Code is quoted **directly from the repository**, with the source file named on
the block so you can open it yourself:

```{.r filename="app/logic/functions.R"}
#' @export
render_info <- function(output) {
  message(format(Sys.time(), digits = 3L), " | ", "----- Rendering '", output, "' UI")
}
```

Boxes flag the technical subtleties worth knowing before you touch the code:

::: {.callout-important title="Implementation detail — for the developer"}
A reactive-timing hazard, a schema invariant, or a reason the code is shaped the
way it is. These usually record a bug that a naive implementation caused, so the
box is worth reading before you "simplify" the thing it describes.
:::

Cross-references such as @sec-architecture are clickable, as are figure
references and citations such as the original MLST description
[@maiden1998mlst]. The full bibliography is on the
[References](references.qmd) page.

## Structure of this book {.unnumbered}

**Part I · The Scaffold** — the application skeleton: boot chain, module system,
the reactive signal bus, the composition patterns and the process boundary to
the bioinformatics toolchain (@sec-architecture); then the SQLite file, its four
families of tables, its keying and its on-load migrations (@sec-database).

**Part II · Component Internals** — the implementation of each pipeline:
scheme management (@sec-tech-schemes), allelic typing (@sec-tech-typing), AMR
screening (@sec-tech-amr), the database browser and custom fields
(@sec-tech-browser), and import/export/staging (@sec-tech-interop).

**Part III · Visualization Internals** — the plot workspace coordinator
(@sec-tech-visualization), the five plot engines (@sec-tech-engines), and the
Analysis Dashboard's persistence (@sec-tech-dashboard).

**Part IV · Operations & Extension** — the planned report function
(@sec-reporting), installation and runtime (@sec-install), the test suite
(@sec-testing), and the conventions for adding to the app (@sec-extending).

**Appendices** — a module reference (@sec-appendix-modules), the full database
schema (@sec-appendix-schema), the pinned external toolchain
(@sec-appendix-tools), and the [References](references.qmd).

## Building this book {.unnumbered}

Both manuals are [Quarto](https://quarto.org) books. From `docs/technical/`:

```bash
quarto render          # build the HTML site (and PDF) into docs/technical/_book/
quarto preview         # live-reload while editing
```

The user manual builds the same way from `docs/manual/`.

*PhyloTrace is intended for research and academic purposes only.*
